name: Lacuna Night
description: Observed on the anniversary of the 2209 BCI Cascade Failure, when a Vantablack Systems firmware push corrupted 340,000 neural interfaces simultaneously, leaving survivors with permanent memory gaps they call 'the lacuna.' Families of victims mark the night by leaving a single unlit candle in their window — a practice that spread from the Shelf outward despite corporate pressure to forget. Vantablack Systems, now absorbed into Hexcor Integrated, has never issued a formal acknowledgment, and any public commemoration larger than a household gathering is technically classified as an 'unlicensed grief assembly' under Hexcor's district licensing codes.
cultural_impact: The unlit candle has become a broader symbol of corporate-caused harm in M88, appearing in protest art and graffiti year-round — a single dark circle against a lit field. Support networks for Cascade survivors, called Lacuna Circles, operate quietly throughout Tier 1 and 2 districts and serve as one of the Shelf's most effective mutual aid structures.
locations: The Lacuna Circle Hub, Muskegon Corridor
story_hooks: A Lacuna survivor's memory gap contains critical evidence of deliberate negligence — and someone inside Hexcor Integrated is willing to kill to keep it fragmented.
The Hollow Voice, an E.L.F. who archived the names of all 340,000 affected, has gone silent for the first time in fifteen years — three days before Lacuna Night.
A player character discovers their own missing memory aligns exactly with the Cascade window, but they have no BCI record — which should be impossible.
origin_event: The 2209 Vantablack Systems BCI Cascade Failure, in which a mandatory firmware update pushed to all registered Vantablack neural interfaces caused catastrophic synaptic feedback, leaving 340,000 survivors with permanent memory lacunae of 6–72 hours.
tier_observations: Tier 1-2: Unlit candles in windows, Lacuna Circle gatherings, shared meals for survivors, quiet reading of names. Tier 3: Some observe privately, especially those with affected family; most avoid public display fearing workplace scrutiny. Tier 4-5: The date is unmarked on any corporate calendar; Hexcor employees are quietly discouraged from acknowledging it at all.
